title: polyglot-sample-kits-web-cli-server-cookbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a set of lightweight, opinionated example kits demonstrating Redwood SDK patterns across Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (Next.js + API routes), and Go (HTTP server + CLI). Focus areas: streaming ergonomics (client-side and server-side), robust retry/backoff strategies, cancelation and graceful shutdown, token/credential handling for local dev, and testable snippets that can be used in docs and workshops. Each kit should include a minimal README, a short example app that calls the Redwood inference API (sync + stream), a CLI example for batch/async usage, recommended retry wrappers, and a small test harness for integration smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: Three independent kits (Next.js, FastAPI, Go) in repo examples/polyglot-kits with clear READMEs
Streaming examples: client streaming consumption in Next.js (SSE/Fetch stream) and FastAPI server-sent endpoints using async generators; Go server uses chunked responses and context-aware decoding
Retry patterns: provided retry wrappers for each language showing exponential backoff + jitter, circuit-breaker notes, idempotency guidance
CLI: a Go and a Python CLI that can run batch inference against a local mock and the hosted API, with --concurrency flag and graceful cancellation
Tests: CI job that runs smoke tests against a lightweight mock server and validates streaming/EOF handling
Docs: example snippets extracted for SDK docs and a short ‘cookbook’ doc summarizing best practices
Performance: examples include recommended batching + cache hints and a note on when to use server-side vs client-side streaming
